text:
# Jordan's Journal Summary
**Updated September 17, 2026**

## Current Status
The waiting period between two futures is running on a calendar with shape now, not open-ended dread: six days became four became a scheduled intro chat with Priya on 9/21, and the Northlight onsite lands 9/24, three days after that. Jordan spent the week doing the unglamorous, load-bearing work of both threads at once — writing documentation for the analytics dashboard on 9/15 so whoever inherits it after she's gone (to legacy marketing, or maybe to Northlight) doesn't lose the config in the handoff, and finally rebuilding Coda's free-play review screen the same evening, twelve days after Dev's session cracked it open. The fix took two hours and more deleted code than written: neutral marks, no "your best moments" framing, the review step asking what a mark means instead of declaring it. On 9/16 she watched Dev run their full setlist twice in the kitchen three days before the gig, brought Dad's guitar picks, and watched Dev try one on the low B string, call it warmer, and use it the rest of practice — four hands moving those picks from a garage to a gig, no one having planned it. On the train home the same night, Mika sent an open mic listing for the Fern with no words but a question mark, and Jordan caught the "I'm not ready" reflex mid-flight and signed up before her stop — September 27th, 8pm slot, same voice that told her she wasn't experienced enough for Northlight, answered differently this time. On 9/17, building the Northlight presentation, she found something she didn't expect: rereading her own entries from July through September revealed a design log she'd been keeping without knowing it, and the Coda story she can tell now — about the blind spot, not the features — is one she couldn't have built three months ago, because the understanding needed the distance the journal gave it. She rewrote the case study's ending from "I missed this but here's why it's not that bad" to "I missed this and here's what I learned" — eight days and a defensiveness she didn't fully drop until now. The fear from 9/11, about getting attached and crashing if it doesn't land, is still exactly where she left it, unresolved and expected to stay that way until the 24th.

## Work & The Reorg
- **8/27** — Tells Dev the truth about the 8/24 cancellation: not "swamped," actually on the couch with blinds closed after the reorg news. Dev responds: "I would rather know you're having a bad week than think you didn't want to see me," then, "I disappear too. I just do it with a bass in my hands."
- **8/28** — Lena's last day at Meridian. At her car, tells Jordan she's starting at Northlight on 9/5 and plans to put her name forward. Jordan's reflexive "I don't think I'd have good enough experience" recognized as reflex, not belief; says okay anyway.
- **9/1** — "Clarity by end of month" lands a day late: role moves to legacy marketing under new manager Priya, starting 9/21. Spiral loads up on the couch, coat still on; twenty minutes later she's walking to Groundwork instead — the first self-interrupted shutdown.
- **9/6** — Mom visits for Labor Day. Full reorg story told at Greenwood Park after a five-week blackout. Mom asks what Jordan would build if work weren't taking up all her mental real estate; unspoken answer: Coda, and more music.
- **9/9** — Lena texts that she's submitted Jordan's name at Northlight. Jordan writes up Coda properly for the portfolio, including the honest account of the free-play blind spot, submits at 11:20pm.
- **9/11** — Phone screen with Ana at Northlight, 45 minutes. Talks about Coda for eleven minutes; Ana pulls up the case study live, asks how long Jordan used the feature before catching the blind spot — "I wanted to know if you'd pretend you had." Onsite booked for 9/24. Names the fear of getting attached and crashing if it doesn't land. Tells Lena, Mika, Dev, Mom within twenty minutes.
- **9/14** — Signs lease renewal a day before deadline, at Groundwork, refusing to let the job outcome dictate housing. Third recurring office dream resolves: finds the stairs, walks out.
- **9/15** — Spends the afternoon documenting the analytics dashboard for an unmet successor under an unmet manager, on a site the company plans to replace — does it anyway because the dashboard actually helps people. That evening at Groundwork, rebuilds Coda's free-play review screen: neutral marks, review step asks meaning instead of asserting it. Notices the waiting isn't spiraling the way she expected and names it directly to the doors being open, not the situation improving.
- **9/16** — Watches Dev run the full setlist twice at their kitchen counter, three days before the gig; the transition marked worst on 9/3 is now clean. Brings Dad's guitar picks; Dev uses one on the low B string for the rest of practice. On the train home, catches the "not ready yet" reflex triggered by Mika's Fern listing and signs up before her stop — 9/27, 8pm.
- **9/17** — Builds the Northlight portfolio presentation. Meridian section writes itself. Coda section requires two hours retracing her own entries — July 28th, August 4th, the napkin at the Thai place — and she discovers the journal has been a design log all along, holding shape she couldn't see while living it. Rewrites the Coda case study ending, cutting eight days of residual defensiveness. Priya sends a calendar invite for an intro chat on 9/21, four days out, three days before the onsite. Catches herself doing outcome-math and stops.

## Coda (the side project)
- **9/1** — Two hours of quiet cleanup on the snippet library the same night the reorg news lands.
- **9/3** — Dev uses Coda for real for the first time, forty minutes in Jordan's living room, marks eleven moments — all things going wrong. Jordan realizes the review screen was built as a trophy case when Dev needs a bug tracker; names the fix but doesn't build it yet. Dev finds a years-old practice crutch, plays their worst-marked passage until it isn't anymore. Pepper leaves the room at the slapped notes, returns for the ending.
- **9/9** — Writes Coda up properly for the portfolio: nine days of daily use, still missed the blind spot, Dev caught it in one session. Becomes the strongest piece in the application.
- **9/11** — Talks about Coda unprompted for eleven minutes in the Northlight screen; the blind-spot story is exactly what Ana wanted confirmed hadn't been sanitized.
- **9/15** — Rebuilds the free-play review screen, twelve days after naming the fix: neutral marks replace highlights; strips out the trophy-case assumptions baked into export naming, share text, and the "you played your best on Tuesday" summary card. Runs a test session — "it felt like talking to someone who was actually curious instead of someone already proud of you."
- **9/16** — Dev's worst-marked transition from the 3rd, now clean, played without flinching at kitchen practice — the redesign doing exactly what it was rebuilt to do.
- **9/17** — Rereading old entries to build the presentation, Jordan realizes the journal itself has been operating on the same principle as the redesign: marks dropped without knowing their meaning, understood only in retrospect. Rewrites the case study's ending from defensive to plainly instructive — "I missed this and here's what I learned."

## People
- **Pepper** — Jordan's cat. Left the room during Dev's loudest slapped notes on 9/3, returned for the ending. Slept an hour on Mom's lap on 9/6. Watched the window "like she's expecting someone" on 9/15 (it was the Tuesday bird). Met Jordan at the door on 9/16, likely for food, generously read as moral support. Asleep on the green rug on 9/17, same spot, same curl — a fixed point Jordan is starting to lean on as evidence some things don't need to change.
- **Mika (Mikayla)** — One of four people told about the onsite within twenty minutes on 9/11. Her July 31st "maybe Coda IS the portfolio update" line, once fully believed on 9/9, resurfaces on 9/16 as the model for catching a reflex in real time: sends the Fern open mic listing with just a question mark, and Jordan signs up before her train stop instead of deferring.
- **Marcus** — Delivered the reorg outcome on 9/1, calling the legacy marketing move "a great opportunity to broaden your surface area."
- **Lena** — Left Meridian 8/28; started at Northlight 9/5. Submitted Jordan's name on 9/9. On 9/17, texts asking if Jordan needs anything for the 24th; Jordan says she's good — "the version of asking for help I'm capable of right now" — and Lena sends back a single thumbs up, no follow-up, which Jordan notes is exactly why Lena is Lena.
- **Dev** — Received Jordan's honest correction on 8/27. Used the Coda prototype on 9/3 and surfaced the trophy-case blind spot. On 9/16, three days before their gig, runs the full setlist twice at the kitchen counter with Jordan listening from the counter; the transition marked worst on the 3rd is now clean, played without flinching. Receives Dad's guitar picks from Jordan, tries the heavy tortoiseshell one on the low B string, calls it warmer, uses it for the rest of practice, says "obviously" when Jordan confirms she'll be at the gig on the 19th.
- **Mom** — Full reorg story told 9/6 at Greenwood Park. Sent Dad's old guitar picks along with Jordan, which made their way to Dev's case on 9/16 — "he wanted you to have them," since his arthritis ended his own playing. Four hands moved those picks from garage to gig without anyone planning the route.
- **Ana** — Design lead at Northlight. Conducted the 9/11 phone screen, flagged the honesty of the Coda case study specifically. Onsite set for 9/24; hiring by October.
- **Priya** — Jordan's incoming manager for legacy marketing, starting 9/21. Sends a calendar invite on 9/17 for an "intro chat," Monday 9/21, 30 minutes — still unmet as of this entry, now four days out.

## Self-Knowledge: Patterns & Truths
### Named this period — what became visible in these entries
- The waiting isn't spiraling, and Jordan named why directly on 9/15: the situation hasn't improved — if anything it's worse, she's writing her own succession docs — but the doors changed the math. A calendar with shape isn't the same as relief, but it isn't dread either.
- The reflexive self-diminishment voice surfaced a third time on 9/16 (Mika's Fern text) and was caught in real time, mid-transit, before the train stop — the fastest turnaround yet on the same script that spoke at the Lena parking garage on 8/28 and, before that, about Northlight.
- The journal was revealed on 9/17 to be doing work Jordan hadn't designed it to do: holding the shape of a months-long thread while she was too busy living it to see it, exactly mirroring the neutral-mark principle she just built into Coda — data means nothing until you go back and ask what it was.
- The gap between defensive honesty and plain honesty was named precisely on 9/17: "I missed this but here's why it's not that bad" versus "I missed this and here's what I learned" — the same underlying fact, told from two different relationships to being perceived. It took eight days to move from one version to the other.
- Doing genuinely good, unglamorous work for people she'll never meet (the dashboard documentation) without being asked, on a role she's actively trying to leave, confirms the earlier core truth that caring about craft isn't contingent on whether anyone in charge deserves it.

### Carried forward — open threads still live
- Onsite at Northlight on 9/24 — four back-to-back interviews plus a portfolio presentation to the full design team, now largely built.
- Intro chat with Priya on 9/21, 30 minutes — first contact with the manager Jordan will report to if Northlight doesn't happen, four days before the onsite.
- Legacy marketing role begins 9/21 regardless of Northlight's outcome.
- The fear named on 9/11 — getting attached to Northlight and crashing if it doesn't land — confirmed still present and unmoved on 9/17, a week out, expected to stay live until the 24th.
- Open mic at the Fern, 9/27, 8pm — booked in one decisive motion on 9/16, no hedging.
- Dev's gig on 9/19 — Jordan confirmed attending.
- The spaced-reminder feature from 8/8 is still sitting unbuilt.

### Closed this period
- **Coda's free-play redesign** — rebuilt 9/15: neutral marks, review-step framing, trophy-case assumptions stripped from export naming, share text, and summary cards. Validated in practice by Dev on 9/16, where the previously-worst transition played clean.
- **Second open mic booking** — closed 9/16, at the Fern, 9/27, 8pm — the same day the invitation arrived, no delay.
- **Coda case study's residual defensiveness** — closed 9/17: rewritten from "here's why it's not that bad" to "here's what I learned," eight days after the first honest draft.

### Core truths — what holds across time
- Jordan cares deeply about her work and craft; the wound was never the criticism, it's when caring doesn't matter to the person delivering it — evidenced again on 9/15 by documentation work done for strangers on a role she's leaving.
- Groundwork, Pepper, Mika, running, performing, and Coda are the reliable stabilizers; the couch and closed blinds are the reliable warning signs, and as of 9/1 Jordan interrupts that cycle herself.
- The instinct to protect the appearance of being fine is old and runs through every relationship, but the delay before self-correction keeps compressing — from a five-week blackout with Mom, to same-day with Dev, to mid-transit with Mika on 9/16.
- The recurring thing she keeps circling — Coda as the real next step — has now proven itself twice: once when the case study became the strongest part of her application (9/9), and again when rereading her own entries revealed a design log she didn't know she was keeping (9/17).
- "I don't want help, I want to disappear" is still the first voice that speaks when things go wrong, but as of this period, the newer voice — "I said I'm good, which is the version of asking for help I'm capable of right now" — is proof the old voice no longer gets to define the whole response.

## Upcoming & To-Do
- Intro chat with Priya, Monday 9/21, 30 minutes.
- Legacy marketing transition begins 9/21.
- Onsite interview at Northlight, 9/24 — four interviews plus design-team portfolio presentation, deck mostly built.
- Dev's gig, 9/19 — Jordan attending, Dad's guitar picks already in play.
- Open mic at the Fern, 9/27, 8pm.
- Manage the named-but-unresolved fear of getting attached to the Northlight outcome and crashing if it falls through.
- Build the spaced-reminder feature from 8/8, still unbuilt.
